new_entities.name: Positional therapy for supine-predominant obstructive sleep apnea
aliases: sleep position therapy for positional OSA
new_entities.description: Positional therapy devices or strategies used to reduce time spent sleeping supine in adults with supine-predominant or positional obstructive sleep apnea.

new_entities.name: Apnea-hypopnea index
new_entities.description: The apnea-hypopnea index, representing the number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep.

edges.effect_quant: Positional therapy lowers event burden in supine-predominant OSA. A 2023 meta-analysis found AHI mean difference -9.19 events/h, and a randomized crossover trial found sleep-position treatment noninferior to APAP within a prespecified 5 events/h margin while improving adherence.
edges.population: adults with positional or supine-predominant obstructive sleep apnea, especially those with relatively low nonsupine event burden
edges.mechanism: Avoiding the supine position reduces posterior tongue and soft-palate collapse, decreasing obstructive events in patients whose apnea is strongly position dependent.
edges.summary: This is a legitimately useful option for positional OSA. It tends to work best when disease is clearly supine driven and less well when obstruction remains substantial in lateral sleep.
edges.caveats: Positional therapy generally does not match APAP for absolute AHI suppression, long-term symptom gains can be modest, and tolerance varies by device design. It is best thought of as phenotype-targeted therapy rather than a universal replacement for PAP.
